lawyer:
MihirKanti Majumder with Hemayet Hossain, Jatirmoya Deb for Jitendra Narayan Deb, Advocates ----- For the Appellants,

parties:
Madaris Ali and others ----- Appellants
Vs
Biswamber Das Being dead his heirs ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
5. Contesting defendant Nos. 1 to 8, 10 and 13 denied the material allegations made in the plaint. They further averred that the plaintiffs suit is not maintainable and barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Their specific case is that Syedunnessa Chowdhurani, Khan Bahadur Gousuddin Ahmed Chowdhury and others did never settle the suit land 40 years ago or at any time with the plaintiffs at an annual rental of half a maund of paddy per kedar or any rent nor they realised any rent from them. Suit land was Khas dakhali land of the said landlords and the same was fallow land even during the land settlement operation and recorded as such in the name of the proforma defendants in the khatians. In 1380 BS principal defendants entered into an agreement with the proforma defendants to purchase the suit land at the rate of Tk. 1250.00 per acre and with the permission of the said owners principal defendant Nos. 14 to 19 sold 24 acre of the suit land in their 14 annas 12 gondas 35 tils share at a consideration of Tk. 30,000 to the principal defendants by a registered sale deed dated 22nd Falgoon, 1381 BS (27.3.75) and the said sellers relinquished all their right, title and interest in the said land in favour of defendants 1 to 13 and the principal defendants have been possessing the same along with 1 anna 7 gondas 3 koras 5 tils shares of proforma defendants 20 and 21 who could not execute and register the sale deed for some difficulties but made over possession of the same to the defendants 1 to 13. Plaintiffs failed to purchase the suit land as the principal defendants offered more money than they had offered and they filed the suit on false allegation of settlement. They had never any title and possession in the suit land. 

 6. Plaintiffs examined 6 witnesses including plaintiff No. 3 Mobarak Ali as PW 1 and also produced and proved some Toka Farags Exts. 1 to 1 (r) in support of their case. Contesting defendants examined 5 witnesses including defendant No. 7 Rowab Ali as DW 1 and also produced and proved some documents such as finally published Khatians Ext. A (2), the government rent receipts Ext. B to B(2) and certified copy of their kabala Ext. C. 

 "In spite of all the defects in" the Toka farags it has now become clear that the plaintiffs have their legs on the suit land and whatever defects crept in the Toka farags have since been perfected by the long user of the suit land by the plaintiffs beyond the statutory period of limitation to the knowledge of the original owners. Khatian Ext A is found to be erroneous and kabala Ext. C is found to have no legal effect. As the plaintiffs have clear title and possession in the suit land the suit is found to be maintainable in the present form." 

 8. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder along with Mr. Hemayet Hossain and Mr. Jotirmoya Deb. learned Advocates, appearing on behalf of Mr. Jitendra Narayan Deb for the appellants, placed before us plaint, written statement, deposition of the witnesses, impugned judgment and other materials on record. The learned Advocate submitted that the plaintiffs failed to establish their alleged claim of settlement of the suit land on the basis of Toka farags Ext. 1 series which are neither in the name of any of the plaintiffs nor any particulars of the suit land mentioned therein. He further submitted that the plaintiffs also failed to establish their alleged adverse possession beyond the statutory period of limitation. He further submitted that the suit land was recorded in the name of predecessor-in-interest of the proforma defendants in finally published Khatians after factual field survey in the locality and the suit land has been recorded as fallow land (layek-patiti/ Layek ura). 

 10. In this case admittedly the suit land belonged to the predecessors-in-interest of the proforma defendants and it was their vacant Khas land and finally published khatians Ext. A series recorded the same in the name of the said landlords as their Khas land. The question in whether the said landlords settled the same with the plaintiffs and or the plaintiffs acquired title therein by adverse possession. 

 13. There is no case of the plaintiffs that they entered into the suit lands forcibly at any point of time to the knowledge of the said landlords, who admittedly reside far away and who has no tahsil office in the locality, denying title of the said landlords. Admittedly suit land was recorded in the name of the landlords Sayedunnessa Chowdhurani and Khan Bahadur Gousuddin Ahmed Chowdhury and others in Khatian Nos. 16 and 112 of mouza Purnakhola and Khatian No. 581 of Mouza Chaluia Exts. A-(2) and the said land has been recorded as fallow land in khas possessions of the said persons. It is admitted by the learned Advocates of both the parties that at the time of acquisition of rent receiving interest under the SAT Act field survey operation for preparation of record of rights under the provisions of Sylhet Tenancy Act 1936 in the suit locality was going on and ultimately the record of rights were prepared and finally published under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as there was no previous settlement operation in the District of Sylhet. Relying on the evidence of PW 1 the learned Advocate for the respondents contended that the said Khatians were wrongly prepared in the name of the landlords. PW 1 in his deposition stated that during last settlement operation they entrusted Morals and Karmacharies of landlords to record the suit land in their name. But in cross-examination he admitted that he has other lands besides the suit land and those were correctly recorded in his name. We have already seen that there was no tahsil office of the Zamindars in the locality and as such entrusting Karmacharies of the Zamindars cannot be relied on. None has corroborated the PW 1 in this respect and he also failed to name the Moral or Karmachari whom the plaintiffs had entrusted for the purpose. Moreover, the plaintiffs never took care to enquire about the Khatians within the period of 12 years from the date of final publication of the Khatians in 1963 and they only enquired about the Khatians in 1975 when they came to know from the principal defendants about the sale of the suit land by the proforma defendants to the principal defendants. The plaintiffs neither claimed to have paid any rent to the Government from 1363 BS till the time of filing the suit in 1382 BS nor produced and proved any rent receipts. In view of the above it is difficult to hold that the said Khatians were not correctly prepared in the name of said Zamindars. Such finally published SA Khatians prepared after field survey operation stand on much better footing and more reliable than the SA Khatians made by merely revising the CS Khatians. 

 15. From the above discussion, it is clear that the plaintiffs' failed to prove their possession in the suit land Plaintiffs claim that they made the suit land fit for cultivation 40 years ago after taking settlement and grew paddy therein is also belied by the entry in the khatians Ext. A series classifying the suit lands as Layak patit layck/ura i.e. follow land in Khas possession of the predecessor of the proforma defendants. It is well settled that possession follows title. Even occasional surreptitious acts of possession on the part of the plaintiffs behind the back of such recorded owners who were admittedly residents of a distant place in the absence of any evidence of forcible entry in the land in denial of title of such owners cannot amount to adverse possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. 

 16. Court below did not assign any reason for finding the khatians Ext. A series to be erroneous and kabala Ext. C to have no legal effect, admittedly Syedunnessa Chowdhurani and others were the owners of the suit land and proforma defendants 14 to 21 as their heirs inherited the same. As the plaintiffs failed to establish their settlement of the same from the said landlords we find no reason how the court below could hold the said khatians in the names of the said landlords to be erroneous and the kabala in favour of the principal defendants to have no legal effect. Had the plaintiffs acquired any title in the suit land they would have paid rent for the same to the Government from 1363 BS after the acquisition of rent receiving interest. They utterly failed to make out any such case of payment of rent to the Government. How could the plaintiffs enjoy the suit land from 1363 BS till the time of filing the suit as claimed by them without paying rent to the Government? Any lay cultivator is quite conscious that he cannot enjoy the land without paying rent to the Government. Had the plaintiffs acquired any interest or title in the suit land they would have endeavored to pay rent to the Government and would have taken steps at the earliest opportunity to get the Khatians corrected in their names. But they have been sitting idle and now have arisen from their deep slumber after lapse of such a long time when the principal defendants purchased the suit land from the proforma defendants. On the other hand, we find from Ext. B series that the contesting defendants paid rents for the years 1379-82 BS vide Ext. B series. These go to show that all previous rents were paid by the recorded owners of the said land as stated by the DW 1 in cross-examination.
